newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-HENMAN MAKES $4,000 PER MINUTE IN GRAND SLAM CUP DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN MAKES $4,000 PER MINUTE IN GRAND SLAM CUP DEBUT.

text.p: Britain's Tim Henman cashed in on his Wimbledon success this year by earning more than $4,000 per minute during a smooth 6-3 6-3 victory over Michael Stich at the lucrative Grand Slam Cup on Tuesday.
But the Briton admitted afterwards he had not given the cash a thought.

Henman, who earned a place as a reserve at the $6 million tournament by reaching the Wimbledon quarter-finals and was then handed a chance to play after late withdrawals, picked up $262,500 for the first-round win.
In just 63 minutes the 22-year-old Briton made more than twice his earnings for the whole of last year. He now has a shot at $431,250 in his next match in the quarter-finals.
"It is nice to play in a tournament with huge amounts of money at stake. But I did not focus on the money today," said Henman.
"I am aware of it. But if you think about it you could get nervous and wouldn't be able to throw the ball up...I play tennis more as a hobby than an occupation."

Henman is the most promising British player for years and the first Briton to play at the Munich tournament, the most lucrative event in the game. Stich said he had the potential to get into the top echelons of the sport.

"He played very well today and is very talented. It really depends on how he deals with the attention," the German said. "He certainly has the potential to go a long way. But there are no guarantees."

Henman deserved the victory after playing some sharp serve-and-volley tennis on the fast indoor surface. He was helped by the fact that Stich, who has been struggling with a shoulder injury, had a particularly poor day.
The former Wimbledon champion struggled to win his own service games as early as the fifth game when Henman just missed out on a break.

The Briton then took the initiative in the set with a break in the seventh game to lead 4-3 after Stich netted a volley. Henman then clinched the set 6-3 after 29 minutes with another break when Stich hit a forehand out of court.
Henman, playing his first match for two weeks, then took a 3-1 lead in the second set after another break in the fourth game and never looked back.
"He made very few mistakes. He made life very difficult for me," Stich said.
